-117.81000,34.02860.name: American Fertility Medical Center Corporation
-117.81000,34.02860.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Thomas Lee, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

77.55009,12.88329.name: Cloudnine Hospital
77.55009,12.88329.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

7.65095,47.42782.name: Katharina Tscharland
7.65095,47.42782.desc: A mapped site of Harlan, a company whose business is animal research, breeding laboratory animals, or both. What this record says is that the company has a site here. It does not say animals are used at this address: a mapped corporate site may be an office, and no regulator publishes a worldwide list of the buildings where the work happens. There is no OpenStreetMap tag for an animal research facility and there should not be one — whether a building runs toxicology studies is not visible from the street, which is the test OpenStreetMap applies to everything it records.

-121.98857,37.54827.name: Neuralink Corp.
-121.98857,37.54827.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-75.88834,41.24010.name: University of Texas Medical Branch - Galveston 301 University BLVD GALVESTON, TX, UNITED STATES
-75.88834,41.24010.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of University of Texas System. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-77.42312,39.43817.name: US Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID)
-77.42312,39.43817.state: 1425 Porter Street, Fort Detrick, Frederick, Maryland 21702-5011, United States
-77.42312,39.43817.company: U.S. Army Medical Research and Materiel Command, Department of Defense
-77.42312,39.43817.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by U.S. Army Medical Research and Materiel Command, Department of Defense. It is categorised as a defense laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 1186 SqM. Operational or announced: 1969. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

77.49366,23.25444.name: National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD)
77.49366,23.25444.state: 162, Manak Vihar, Patel Nagar, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh 462022, India, India
77.49366,23.25444.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-71.08850,42.36250.name: Beam Therapeutics
-71.08850,42.36250.desc: Base editing changes a single DNA letter without cutting the double helix, which avoids the breaks that cause most unintended damage from earlier methods. Roughly half of known disease-causing mutations are single-letter changes, so the technique addresses more conditions than any other editing chemistry — and because it makes a change indistinguishable from a natural variant, it is also the hardest to detect afterwards in anything it is used on.

-77.11090,38.88160.name: American Seed Trade Association
-77.11090,38.88160.desc: The US seed industry association, and the main lobby on plant variety protection, seed patents and state-level labelling. It is also the body that has argued consistently that edited crops should not be regulated as engineered ones — a position now written into US policy, which makes this association's advocacy one of the more consequential on the map.

-77.11090,38.88160.name: Ceres Nanosciences / environmental RNA monitoring
-77.11090,38.88160.desc: Technologies for detecting genetic material in water and soil samples. Environmental DNA methods could find engineered sequences in a river or a field margin without knowing in advance what to look for, and the capability is being funded for pathogen surveillance rather than for watching releases.

-89.47500,43.09000.name: Promega
-89.47500,43.09000.desc: Makes the enzymes and assay systems that molecular biology runs on, and the forensic DNA kits used by police laboratories. The same catalogue serves a university bench and a criminal investigation, and the company is privately held with a founder-set structure that has kept it out of the consolidation that took most of its peers.

-77.03200,38.88650.name: USDA Plant Variety Protection Office
-77.03200,38.88650.desc: Grants US plant variety certificates, which sit alongside utility patents on the same crops — and the two carry different rules. A variety certificate preserves a farmer's right to save seed for their own use; a utility patent does not, which is what Bowman v. Monsanto turned on. Which instrument covers a variety therefore decides what a grower may lawfully do, and the register says which.

-0.13200,51.50600.name: National academies of science — advice to governments
-0.13200,51.50600.state: London — Royal Society, Carlton House Terrace
-0.13200,51.50600.desc: Academies are asked by governments for a position before a law is drafted, which is earlier and less visible than the regulatory assessment of any single application. Their reports are published and their working groups are named, so it is possible to see who advised and on what basis — and several national academies have taken positions on gene editing that their own regulators had not yet reached.
